event.summary: Removed output cleanup barriers are unnecessary for grid-only attachments
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether removing process-reaping barriers and joining attachment output tasks sequentially could leave future terminal attachments blocked or conflict with a surviving old output client. Details: the changed connection cleanup signals every extracted attachment before joining (connection.rs:787-792); terminals.rs:478-483 joins the actual GridSender task, and grid_stream.rs:937-965 races stream.run against shutdown.changed with the shutdown branch biased first. The stream future is dropped before report_forwarder_end, which schedules map mutations in separate tasks rather than awaiting the attachments lock. The replacement output task owns no external tmux client; terminals.rs:438-441 says 'it holds no external process, so it stops at once.' Thus the removed reaping barrier protected the retired tmux resources rather than a surviving grid resource, and sequential joining after signal-all does not serialize the start of shutdown. Suggested bucket: other (not a finding). Confidence: confirmed by source; no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation; no process remains for this removed barrier to protect. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route from this concern; it concerned blocked attachment cleanup. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. Caveat: this conclusion covers the assigned connection cleanup and GridSender shutdown interface, not terminal-host runtime persistence internals.

event.summary: Output joins do not wait on the attachment map
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Replacing tmux process-reaping barriers with direct grid-task joins does not establish a blocked replacement attachment or output-join deadlock. Details: connection cleanup signals every extracted attachment before joining (connection.rs:787-792). join_forwarder awaits only the GridSender handle (terminals.rs:478-483). GridSender::run (grid_stream.rs:937-965) biases shutdown.changed before stream.run and drops the stream future before calling report_forwarder_end. The dispatcher (connection.rs:1272-1330) is synchronous: natural and stall endings spawn arbiters that acquire attachments separately; Requested/ClientGone do nothing. Thus an output task awaited while attachments is locked never waits for an arbiter to take that lock. Removed barriers concern external tmux output-client processes; the grid sender owns no such process. Suggested bucket: other; no established regression. Confidence: confirmed source analysis, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation of the output-join/process-reaping concern; no parent drop accepted. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work consequence for this output-join concern. possible_cover: parent reports g117/g125 independently checked that the GridSender dispatcher does not await the attachment lock. Material caveat: this does not settle input-pump cancellation lifetime, now separately retained as finding l1. This synthesis revision makes the output/input distinction and independent interface check explicit; it does not rely on those peers as a substitute for the source read.

event.summary: Natural detach releases attachment ownership before dropping its input pump
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: A failed or naturally ended terminal attachment may leave previously queued input able to reach the terminal after a replacement viewer acquires control. Details: detach_naturally removes old, moves only old.forwarder into join_forwarder, then drops the attachments guard and calls notify_detached; old.input remains a partially moved local until the async block ends. The previous implementation explicitly dropped backend before dropping attachments. HostAttach::drop sends the cancellation signal (grid_stream.rs:1169-1175); Pump::run continues handing queued input into the runtime until cancellation (1201-1233). Exact missing premise: whether this ordering permits a meaningful input handoff after a shipped replacement attachment becomes active, beyond input the terminal runtime already accepted before detach; inspect attach installation and notification paths, and compare existing input lifetime contracts. Suggested bucket: highest if stale-viewer input can cross the control boundary (terminal input can execute commands), otherwise high/other according to established effect. Confidence: unresolved source lead, not executed. proposed_drop: false. Could-be-highest: yes, pending the ownership/handoff premise. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. Next checks: pinned attach handler, notify_detached, original host input wrapper, and input lifetime contract. No reproduction requested or performed.

event.summary: Natural-detach input drop ordering has no established live-terminal route
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. Checks/results: notify_detached (connection.rs:1110-1129) never awaits; HostAttach::drop signals cancellation and Pump::run prioritizes it (grid_stream.rs:1169-1233). The caller cannot submit further frames through the removed map entry (connection.rs:507-513). The remaining route is send's encoding-error branch (818-822), expressly documented as 'A message that does not encode is a sender bug'. Source checks of grid_output row conversion and packing, protocol limits and the emulator's combining-character cap found no legal output that establishes that premise: dimensions cap at 1000, per-cell text at 68 bytes, links at 256 with bounded id/URI, and packing drops links to fit. A new encoding bug cannot be assumed for this finding. Runtime input already handed over is explicitly permitted to outlive a viewer by grid_stream.rs:155-160: 'Input it handed over is the runtime's, and is written in order before anything a replacement attachment sends.' SPEC_impl.md:2290-2294 similarly says dropping a receipt does not take accepted input back (implementation source is hosts/terminal.rs:2290-2294; this is a source contract, not a SPEC citation). Suggested bucket: other for the unsupported lifetime concern, not a verified impact. Confidence: source-validated narrowing; no execution. proposed_drop: no established shipped route from the lifetime gap to executable stale input on a still-usable runtime. Could-be-highest: yes, original suspected consequence was old-viewer command execution crossing a replacement's control boundary; it would need a legal StreamFailed encoding path while the input runtime remains live, and actual queued-input reordering. Neither is established. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. Caveat: cancellation itself is cooperative even before this commit, and neither old nor new cleanup joins the input pump. A separate proven encoder defect or a changed input-pump lifecycle would require revisiting this candidate.

event.summary: Natural detach can leave the old viewer's input pump live after takeover
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: When a terminal viewer's output fails while its terminal still runs, input queued by that viewer can survive until after another viewer takes control, allowing old keystrokes to land among the new viewer's commands. Details: detach_naturally removes old, moves only old.forwarder into join_forwarder, releases the global attachments lock, calls notify_detached, and only at the async block's end drops old.input (connection.rs:1510-1519). The parent explicitly dropped backend before releasing that lock. This creates a new cross-worker scheduling gap in which replacement attach can install a new input pump under the released lock (handlers.rs:1729-1969), while the old pump has not even received its cancellation signal. HostAttach::drop signals it (grid_stream.rs:1169-1175); Pump::run/handle (1201-1278) can otherwise continue dequeuing and handing input to the host. An old pump that had not yet polled its queued input before this unlock can now do so after replacement admission; this is distinct from the unchanged already-polled handover race reported by the caller as g119/c4. A source-established live-terminal encoding-failure route exists: the authenticated terminal WebSocket accepts u16 size query fields (helm/terminal.rs:198-202) and resize controls (627-630,910-913), client.rs:4153-4212/4388-4403 forwards them unchanged, supervisor handlers.rs:1910/2081 calls HostTerminal::resize, and host Size::is_valid allows 1..=10000 (terminal-host/protocol.rs:102,135-145). A 1001-column size is valid for the running host, but grid_output::screen (319-363) copies that size to Hello/Frame and GridOutput::validate rejects dimensions over 1000 (proto/grid.rs:446,1294,1323). GridStream::send returns StreamFailed while the input runtime remains live (818-822), and report_forwarder_end routes that to detach_naturally (connection.rs:1292-1307). Thus no hypothetical encoder bug, giant link, or counter exhaustion is needed. A replacement attaching at an ordinary size repairs the size and can drive the same runtime. Suggested fix: explicitly drop the removed attachment's input side before releasing attachments, preserving the pre-change cancellation-before-new-admission ordering; this does not purport to fix the separate pre-existing midpoll race. Contract: the grid input module says 'The pump ends with the attachment' and drops input not yet handed to the runtime (grid_stream.rs:155-160). The connection ownership guard itself remains intact; this concern is input already queued at that guard, not new frames bypassing it. Suggested bucket: highest if authenticated scripted/API terminal viewers count as the shipped control route; terminal input can execute commands. If the caller applies the priority rule to require generation by the bundled GUI specifically, bucket other for the established cancellation-order regression and retain the potentially highest consequence explicitly: grid-terminal.js:246-250 clamps that GUI's fitted size to 1000, so ordinary GUI resize alone does not trigger this route. Confidence: confirmed source ordering and accepted API encoding-failure route; concurrency consequence is source analysis, not execution. proposed_drop: false. Could-be-highest: yes; original consequence is old-viewer command execution crossing the replacement's exclusive-input boundary. possible_cover: g119/c4, caller-reported, covers only pre-range already-polled handover; not this changed late-drop gap. Caveats: natural host Gone/Unavailable/runtime-end verdicts cannot write through a replacement runtime (old InputSequence holds Weak<old Inner>); InputFailed already stopped its pump. The size-range mismatch is an existing interface premise, not claimed as newly introduced by this removal. Already runtime-accepted input is expressly allowed to outlive the viewer and is not the defect. No tests, builds or reproductions run. No parent drop accepted.

event.summary: Natural detach can leave old viewer input live after replacement admission
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: If a viewer's output fails while its terminal still runs, queued input from that viewer can reach the terminal after another viewer takes control, potentially mixing old keystrokes into the new viewer's commands. Details: connection.rs:1510-1519 removes old, moves only old.forwarder into join_forwarder, drops attachments, calls notify_detached, then drops the unmoved old.input at the async block's end. The parent revision connection.rs:2172-2191 explicitly dropped backend before dropping attachments. Rust's partial-move lifetime therefore leaves cancellation unsignalled after new admission becomes possible. HostAttach::drop sends cancellation (grid_stream.rs:1169-1175); Pump::run prioritizes it at poll boundaries but otherwise keeps handling queued input (1201-1278). The supervisor uses a multi-threaded Tokio Runtime::new (core.rs:16022); detach can be preempted after releasing attachments while another worker installs a replacement (handlers.rs:1729-1969). An old pump not yet polled before that release can then start handing over its queued input after replacement admission. This is distinct from the caller-reported g119/c4 race: cancellation cannot preempt a pump already executing a poll, which existed before this commit. The suggested fix is to drop old.input before releasing attachments, restoring the previous cancellation-before-admission order; this does not claim to fix g119/c4. Supervisor handle_attach/handle_resize pass them to terminal.resize (handlers.rs:1910,2081), whose Size::is_valid permits 1..=10000 (terminal-host/protocol.rs:102,135-145). Runtime::turn applies an accepted size without ending the runtime (hosts/terminal.rs:3082-3098). A valid host size of 1001 columns is copied by grid_output::screen into grid output (319-363), but GridOutput::validate refuses Hello/Frame dimensions over 1000 (proto/grid.rs:446,1294,1323). GridStream::send returns StreamFailed on that encoding failure (818-822); report_forwarder_end routes it to detach_naturally (connection.rs:1292-1307). Thus this route needs no separate hypothetical encoder defect, giant link or counter exhaustion. A replacement viewer can attach at <=1000 columns to repair the terminal size and use the same live runtime. Extra checks: Gone/Unavailable stop runtime work and finish resolves unsent input NotSent and drains/closes input_rx (hosts/terminal.rs:3028-3053,4365-4377); InputSequence holds Weak<old Inner> (1519-1522), so it does not retarget a newly adopted runtime; InputFailed comes from a stopped pump. Styles use defined flags/colors, screen cursors clamp, clipboard parts are bounded, row text is capped at 68 bytes per cell and links at 256 with id/URI bounds; Frame.rev/History numbers separately cap at 2^53-1. No short route to counter exhaustion was found, and it is unnecessary to this size-based route. Contract: grid_stream.rs:155-160 says 'The pump ends with the attachment' and drops input not handed to the runtime. Runtime-accepted input is expressly allowed to outlive a viewer; that is not this defect. Suggested bucket: highest for the source-established authenticated terminal API route, because stale terminal input can execute commands across the exclusive-control boundary. Could-be-highest: yes, preserving the original command-execution consequence. Material priority caveat: the bundled GUI's proposeSize clamps dimensions to 1000 (grid-terminal.js:246-250), so that GUI alone does not generate the large-size trigger. This route is through accepted API/scripted-client input; if the caller requires a bundled-GUI-generated route under the priority rule, retain that missing premise and rebucket by the established cancellation-order defect rather than silently dropping the original consequence. Confidence: confirmed source ordering and accepted API failure route; scheduling consequence is source analysis, not observed execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: caller-reported g119/c4 covers unchanged already-polled handover, not this distinct new lifetime gap. Caveats: the size-range mismatch predates this patch and is used only as an established trigger, not reported as newly introduced here.
